subject: Chemistry
description: Allotropes, hydrocarbons, functional groups, everyday substances

questions.explanation: Allotropes: same element, different structural forms. Carbon allotropes: diamond (tetrahedral sp³), graphite (planar sp²), fullerenes (C60), graphene, carbon nanotubes, amorphous carbon. Allotropes differ in physical properties (hardness, conductivity) despite same element.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.explanation: Methane — CH₄, 1 carbon, simplest hydrocarbon. Main component of natural gas. Potent greenhouse gas (GWP ~28 over 100 years). Alkane series: CH₄, C₂H₆, C₃H₈, C₄H₁₀... (CnH₂n+₂).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Match the FUNCTIONAL GROUP with its class. A. -OH.  B. -COOH.  C. -CHO.  D. -NH₂. List-II: 1. Alcohol.  2. Carboxylic acid.  3. Aldehyde.  4. Amine.
questions.explanation: -OH = alcohol (e.g., ethanol). -COOH = carboxylic acid (e.g., acetic acid). -CHO = aldehyde (e.g., formaldehyde). -NH₂ = amine (e.g., methylamine). Others: -C=O (ketone), -OR (ether), -CN (nitrile).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The chemical formula of ACETIC ACID (vinegar) is:
questions.explanation: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid) = CH₃COOH. Vinegar is ~4-8% acetic acid. HCOOH = formic acid (ants, stinging nettles). C₂H₅OH = ethanol (alcohol).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: Which of the following is a POLYMER?
questions.explanation: Polymer = long-chain molecule from repeating monomer units. Polythene — from ethene monomers. Natural polymers: rubber, cellulose, proteins, DNA. Synthetic: polyester, nylon, PVC, Bakelite.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The process of HYDROGENATION is used to convert:

options.option_text: Vegetable oils to solid fats (vanaspati ghee)

questions.explanation: Hydrogenation — addition of H₂ across C=C double bonds in the presence of Ni (or Pt/Pd) catalyst. Converts unsaturated vegetable oils → saturated solid fats (vanaspati). Downside: creates trans fats associated with heart disease.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.stem: The PUREST form of carbon is:
questions.explanation: Fullerene (C60, 'buckminsterfullerene' or 'bucky ball') — purely C₆₀ molecule, no impurities. Discovered 1985 by Kroto, Curl, Smalley (Nobel Chemistry 1996). Graphite and diamond are also pure carbon in crystalline form, but fullerene's well-defined molecular cage gives it 'highest purity' distinction in teaching contexts.
